abs-business-open-2027.about:
ABS Business Open 2027 is a global pitch contest run by Aoba-BBT's Attackers Business School to mark its 30th anniversary. It has three divisions: High School (under 18, Japan residents only), University (students 18+, including graduate students) and General (professionals and entrepreneurs).

Open Entry is available to anyone not at a partner university (BBT University, Bond University, CTBC Business School, University of the Philippines), with no nationality or residency limits for the university and general divisions. Applicants submit a 9-slide business summary in English; shortlisted entrants send a 5-minute pitch video, and finalists pitch at the Global Final in Tokyo on 13 March 2027.

The University division Grand Prize is USD 1,000 plus a startup support programme (the General division offers USD 20,000 investment). Entry is free and finalists get partial travel and accommodation support.
highlights: Free entry, open to students of any nationality
Final in Tokyo with partial travel support
University Grand Prize USD 1,000 + startup support
abs-business-open-2027.eligibility: University division: students aged 18+ (undergraduate or graduate), individuals or teams, any nationality. Students of partner universities apply via their school.
how_to_apply: Complete the online entry form in English by 31 January 2027.
Upload a business summary PDF (1 cover + 8 content slides, with speaker notes).
If you pass the February document screening, submit a ~5-minute pitch video.
Finalists pitch at the Global Final in Tokyo on 13 March 2027.
abs-business-open-2027.costs: Free. Finalists receive partial travel and accommodation support (capped).

aiseef-2027.about:
ASEAN Innovative Science Environmental and Entrepreneur Fair (AISEEF) is an international science, invention and innovation fair run by the Indonesian Young Scientist Association (IYSA), which organises project competitions for students from elementary school to university in Indonesia and with partners in many countries. AISEEF has run since 2020 and focuses on innovation, environmental awareness and entrepreneurial thinking as tools for real change.

Participants (individually or in small teams) submit a research or invention project in one of the categories (entrepreneur, social sciences, environment sciences, innovation sciences, industrial application, informatics, robotics and AI, life sciences, physics, energy and engineering) and present it to a panel of judges, either in person in Indonesia or online. Medals (gold, silver, bronze) and special awards are given, and all participants receive certificates.

It is an accessible way for school and university students to present their first research project internationally. The guidebook on the official website gives the venue, fees and rules.
highlights: Hybrid: compete online or in person in Indonesia
Open to elementary, secondary and university students
Medals, special awards and certificates
aiseef-2027.eligibility: Students from elementary school to university, from any country, individually or in teams with a supervisor (see guidebook for team size and age categories).
how_to_apply: Read the AISEEF guidebook on the official website.
Register online through the official registration link before the deadline.
Pay the registration fee for online or offline participation as set out in the guidebook.
Submit your project materials (abstract, poster/video) and present to the judges on the event dates.
aiseef-2027.costs: Registration fee varies by online or offline participation and nationality; see the official guidebook. Travel and accommodation for offline participants are self-funded.

amgen-scholars-asia-2027.about:
The Amgen Scholars Asia Program places undergraduates in research groups at five host institutions: Kyoto University (4 June – 5 August 2027), the University of Tokyo (3 June – 5 August), the National University of Singapore (31 May – 5 August), Tsinghua University in Beijing (4 June – 5 August) and IIIT Hyderabad (6 June – 5 August). Scholars work full-time on a research project under a faculty mentor, mostly in the life sciences, chemistry, bioengineering and related fields.

All Asia scholars meet at a symposium (held at the University of Tokyo in 2026) to present their work and hear from academic and industry scientists; travel to and board at the symposium are covered. Each host provides support for housing, food and travel (details vary by host). There is no citizenship requirement: applicants must be enrolled at a university in Asia as defined by the UN, which includes Georgia, Qatar and the rest of West Asia.
highlights: Full-time research at Kyoto, Tokyo, NUS, Tsinghua or IIIT Hyderabad
Funded by host support plus a covered Asia symposium
Open to students at universities in Georgia, Qatar and across Asia
amgen-scholars-asia-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled at a bachelor's-granting university in Asia (UN definition, which includes Georgia, Qatar, the Gulf and Türkiye), who have completed at least their first year by the time the programme starts and will return for at least one more term afterwards. Strong academic record, interest in a PhD and English proficiency (e.g. TOEFL iBT 72, IELTS 5.5, Cambridge FCE or TOEIC equivalents if English is not the first language). No citizenship requirement; scholars arrange visas.
how_to_apply: Choose one host on the Asia page of amgenscholars.com (you may only be placed at one Asian host)
Apply through that host's online application between 1 November 2026 and 1 February 2027
Prepare an official transcript, a recommendation letter, a personal statement and an English test score if needed
Selected scholars arrange visas and attend the Asia symposium
amgen-scholars-asia-2027.costs: No fee. Each host provides support for housing, food and travel (amounts vary by host); symposium travel and board are covered.

amgen-scholars-europe-2027.about:
The Amgen Scholars Programme gives undergraduates a full-time, hands-on research experience in the labs of leading institutions. In Europe it is hosted by ETH Zürich (2 July – 4 September 2027), Institut Pasteur in Paris (1 July – 4 September), Karolinska Institutet in Stockholm (21 June – 13 August, plus the symposium), LMU Munich (2 July – 4 September) and the University of Cambridge (5 July – 4 September). Each scholar joins a research group and works on a project in biology, chemistry, biomedicine or related sciences under a faculty mentor.

All European scholars meet at the University of Cambridge in early September for the Europe Symposium, where they present their work and hear from scientists in academia and industry; travel and board for the symposium are covered. Housing, food and travel support for the summer itself are provided by each host (details vary). There is no citizenship requirement: what matters is being enrolled at a university in a European Higher Education Area (Bologna Process) country, which includes Georgia.
highlights: 8–10 weeks of real lab research at ETH, Pasteur, Karolinska, LMU or Cambridge
Funded: host support for housing/living plus a fully covered symposium in Cambridge
No citizenship requirement; you can apply to several hosts
amgen-scholars-europe-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate students enrolled at a university in a country of the European Higher Education Area / Bologna Process (this includes Georgia and Türkiye; Qatar is not included), usually in the second year of a three-year bachelor's or the second or third year of a four-year/integrated programme at the time of application, who will not have completed their first degree before the programme. A strong academic record and an interest in a PhD are expected. No citizenship requirement; scholars arrange their own visas.
how_to_apply: Read the Europe page on amgenscholars.com and choose one or more host institutions
Apply through each host's own online application between 1 November 2026 and 1 February 2027
Typical requirements: official transcript, a letter of recommendation and a personal statement or essay
Selected scholars arrange visas and join the Cambridge symposium in September
amgen-scholars-europe-2027.costs: No fee. Each host provides financial support for housing, food and travel (amounts vary by host); travel to and board at the Cambridge symposium are covered by the programme.

amt-computational-algorithmic-thinking-2.about:
The Computational and Algorithmic Thinking (CAT) competition, run by the Australian Mathematics Trust, tests logical and algorithmic problem solving without requiring any programming. The 2027 competition is held at school from 18 to 20 May 2027 (60 minutes, paper or online).

Divisions: Upper Primary (Years 5–6), Junior (7–8), Intermediate (9–10) and Senior (11–12). International schools can enter, with an earlier deadline for printed papers. Strong CAT results are a good stepping stone to informatics olympiads.

Every participant gets a certificate; top performers receive awards.
highlights: No programming required
Paper or online, at your school
Good preparation for informatics olympiads
amt-computational-algorithmic-thinking-2.eligibility: School students in Years 5–12, entered by their school (Australia, New Zealand or international).
how_to_apply: Ask your school to register through the AMT admin portal.
International printed entries by 23 April 2027; online entries by 14 May 2027.
Sit the paper at school between 18 and 20 May 2027.
Receive certificates and results from AMT.

big-science-competition-2027.about:
The Big Science Competition is run each May by Australian Science Innovations (ASI), the not-for-profit that runs the Australian Science Olympiads. It is a 50-minute online test of scientific thinking, reading of data and problem solving rather than memorised facts, for students in Years 7 to 10.

It is open to students globally; recent participants have come from Singapore, Hong Kong, Malaysia and New Zealand as well as Australia. In 2026 it ran from 4 to 15 May; the 2027 window is expected in May again.

All students receive results and certificates, and high scorers can be invited towards the Australian Science Olympiad pathway (for eligible Australian students).
highlights: Open to students worldwide
Tests scientific reasoning, not memorisation
Certificates for all participants
big-science-competition-2027.eligibility: Students in Years 7–10 (grades 7–10), entered through their school or a teacher; open globally.
how_to_apply: Ask your science teacher to register the school with ASI for 2027.
Subscribe to ASI programme updates for the 2027 dates.
Sit the online test at school in the May window.
Receive results and certificates.
big-science-competition-2027.costs: Per-student entry fee set by ASI (see the 2027 registration information).

chiang-mai-university-seed-spring-2027.about:
SEED (Sustainable English Experiential Discovery) is run by the Language Institute of Chiang Mai University as part of its Global Sustainability School. The spring 2027 edition runs from 7 to 20 February 2027 in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand.

Participants study English and public speaking while learning about SDG 6 (water security), climate change, flooding and community resilience. The programme includes Lanna culture, Thai cooking, a visit to Doi Suthep, a Khantoke dinner and a CMU student buddy.

It is open to international undergraduate and postgraduate students (and faculty-led groups); no sustainability background is needed.
highlights: Sustainability and English skills in northern Thailand
CMU student buddy and cultural activities
13 nights accommodation included
chiang-mai-university-seed-spring-2027.eligibility: International undergraduate and postgraduate students (individuals or groups). No sustainability background required.
how_to_apply: Read the programme details on the Global Sustainability School page.
Submit the online Apply Now form.
Wait for confirmation and payment instructions from LICMU.
Arrange flights, insurance and visa for Thailand.
chiang-mai-university-seed-spring-2027.costs: THB 37,500 including programme fees, 13 nights accommodation, logistics and some meals. Flights and insurance extra.

chiang-mai-university-wow-program-2027.about:
Women Leading Our Connected World (WOW) is a Chiang Mai University Language Institute programme focused on women's empowerment, leadership and intercultural communication, run from 28 August to 13 September 2027 in Chiang Mai.

It is part of CMU's Global Sustainability School, which welcomes international undergraduate and postgraduate students and study-abroad groups; no background in the topic is needed.

Applications open on 1 March 2027.
highlights: Women's leadership and empowerment focus
Intercultural communication in northern Thailand
Accommodation and logistics included
chiang-mai-university-wow-program-2027.eligibility: International undergraduate and postgraduate students. Check the programme page for any specific criteria when applications open.
how_to_apply: Check the Global Sustainability School page from 1 March 2027.
Submit the online application form.
Pay the programme fee once accepted.
Book flights and arrange your Thai visa if needed.
chiang-mai-university-wow-program-2027.costs: THB 45,000 including programme fees, 16 nights accommodation, logistics and some meals. Flights extra.

doshisha-summer-session-2027.about:
Doshisha University's Center for Japanese Language and Culture runs a summer session in Kyoto each year (6 July – 5 August in 2026), combining intensive Japanese classes with cultural studies in one of Japan's most historic cities.

It is designed for students with JLPT N4 to N2 level (or equivalent); complete beginners and N1-level learners are not eligible. Applicants must be enrolled in, or graduates of, a university and able to obtain a visa. Places are limited to about 20.

The 2027 session is expected to open for applications in mid-January 2027 with a mid-March deadline.
highlights: Intensive Japanese in Kyoto
Small group (about 20 students)
Open to university students and graduates worldwide
doshisha-summer-session-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate or graduate students, or university graduates, with JLPT N4–N2 or equivalent Japanese; must be able to get a visa if required.
how_to_apply: Check the Summer Session page for the 2027 call (expected January).
Apply online with passport copy, motivation letter and letter of consent.
Receive results in late March.
Pay the programme fee in early April to complete registration.
doshisha-summer-session-2027.costs: 2026 fee: JPY 250,000. Accommodation, travel and living costs extra.

elsa-delegations-november-call-2026.about:
ELSA holds special consultative status with UN ECOSOC, consultative status with UNESCO and participatory status with the Council of Europe. Through ELSA Delegations it sends over 300 law students and young lawyers a year to sessions of bodies such as the Commission on the Status of Women, the Commission for Social Development, UNCITRAL, WIPO committees and the Council of Europe's World Forum for Democracy, typically five delegates per session.

Calls open about every two months, each listing roughly 15 sessions; the next call opens on 23 November 2026 at 18:00. Delegates observe real negotiations, attend side events, meet diplomats and report back. Only ELSA members and alumni aged 18+ can apply; ELSA has national groups in 40+ countries including Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Ukraine and Türkiye.
highlights: Observe real UN and Council of Europe sessions
About 15 sessions per call, 5 delegates each
Strong CV boost for international law careers
elsa-delegations-november-call-2026.eligibility: ELSA members and alumni aged 18+ (join your local ELSA group first). Selection by ELSA International criteria; English required.
how_to_apply: Become a member of your local ELSA group
Read the selection criteria on the ELSA Delegations site
When the call opens on 23 Nov 2026, choose sessions and submit your application before that call's deadline
Selected delegates are informed by email within 1-2 weeks
elsa-delegations-november-call-2026.costs: No ELSA fee stated; delegates usually cover their own travel and accommodation (some local groups offer support).

elsa-helga-pedersen-moot-court-2027.about:
The Helga Pedersen Moot Court Competition (HPMCC), formerly the European Human Rights Moot Court Competition, is organised by ELSA with the Council of Europe. In its 15th edition, teams of 2-4 law students from the same university write two written submissions (applicant and respondent) on a fictitious case under the European Convention on Human Rights, due 10 January 2027.

Teams then plead at mandatory Regional Rounds; the 18 best teams qualify for the Final Oral Round in Strasbourg, held at the European Court of Human Rights and the Council of Europe. The best team wins a one-month study visit at the European Court of Human Rights; the best orator wins a study visit at the Council of Europe Liaison Office in Brussels.

The competition is open to law students from Council of Europe member states and beyond (check the rules), including Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Ukraine and Türkiye.
highlights: Final pleadings at the European Court of Human Rights
Winning team gets a one-month study visit at the ECtHR
Academic Board of leading human rights lawyers
elsa-helga-pedersen-moot-court-2027.eligibility: Teams of 2-4 law students from the same university, up to 2 coaches. Working language English (check rules for French).
how_to_apply: Form a team of 2-4 law students from your university
Register via the official form and pay the EUR 100 team fee
Submit up to three clarification questions
Submit the two written submissions by 10 January 2027
Plead at a Regional Round; top 18 teams go to Strasbourg
elsa-helga-pedersen-moot-court-2027.costs: Team registration EUR 100; Regional Round EUR 100 per participant (EUR 120 per coach); Final Oral Round EUR 160 per participant (EUR 185 per coach). Travel at own cost.

elsa-john-h-jackson-moot-court-2027.about:
The John H. Jackson Moot Court Competition (formerly the ELSA Moot Court Competition on WTO Law) reaches its 25th edition in 2026-27. Teams write two written submissions (complainant and respondent, max 35 pages each) on a fictitious WTO dispute published on 16 September 2026, then plead orally before panels of WTO and trade-law professionals.

Regional Rounds: Kraków (24-27 Feb 2027) and Brussels (3-6 Mar 2027) for Europe, plus rounds in Kolkata, Hanoi, Santiago de Chile and Windhoek. The best 24 teams worldwide reach the Final Oral Round at WTO headquarters in Geneva, 15-19 June 2027. Ranking combines oral pleadings (60%) and written submissions (40%).

Open to law students worldwide (one team per law faculty). ELSA International offers financial aid covering half or all of the registration fee; apply with CV and motivation letter by 6 November 2026.
highlights: Final round at WTO headquarters in Geneva
Regional rounds in Kraków and Brussels for European teams
Financial aid available for the registration fee
elsa-john-h-jackson-moot-court-2027.eligibility: Teams of 2-4 law students enrolled at an accredited law faculty anywhere in the world; one team per university/faculty; up to 2 coaches. Working language English.
how_to_apply: Form a team of 2-4 law students from the same faculty
Register through the official registration form (fee EUR 250 per team)
Apply for financial aid by 6 Nov 2026 if needed
Submit clarification questions and written submissions by the official timeline
Plead at your assigned Regional Round
elsa-john-h-jackson-moot-court-2027.costs: Registration EUR 250 per team; Regional Round EUR 160 per participant (EUR 180 per coach); Final Oral Round EUR 700 per team plus EUR 180 per coach. Travel at own cost; financial aid for the registration fee available.

eyp-ireland-leinster-regional-session-20.about:
EYP Ireland runs regional conferences each year for senior-cycle students, from which delegates are selected for the National Session and EYP international events. The 2026/27 Leinster Regional Selection Conference takes place in Dublin, 29-31 January 2027. Delegates do teambuilding, committee work on a European policy topic and a General Assembly debate of the resolutions, chaired by young volunteers from across Europe.

The session is residential (accommodation for Friday and Saturday nights) for those who need it. Fees are EUR 60 non-residential or EUR 75 residential, paid in advance, then each delegate registers individually through the form.
highlights: Selection route to EYP Ireland National Session and international sessions
Residential weekend with European volunteer chairs
Affordable: EUR 60-75
eyp-ireland-leinster-regional-session-20.eligibility: Senior-cycle secondary-school students (about 15-18) in Ireland, in school delegations or individually. Officials from other countries apply via the EYP Members Platform.
how_to_apply: Ask your school to register a delegation or contact the head organisers
Pay the participation fee in advance
Register individually through the session registration form
Prepare with the topic overviews sent before the session
eyp-ireland-leinster-regional-session-20.costs: EUR 60 non-residential / EUR 75 residential (accommodation Friday-Saturday). Late payment admin fee EUR 10; no refunds within a week of the session.

eyp-ireland-munster-regional-session-202.about:
EYP Ireland runs regional conferences each year for senior-cycle students, from which delegates are selected for the National Session and EYP international events. The 2026/27 Munster Regional Selection Conference takes place in Cork, 13-16 February 2027. Delegates do teambuilding, committee work on a European policy topic and a General Assembly debate of the resolutions, chaired by young volunteers from across Europe.

The session is residential (accommodation for Friday and Saturday nights) for those who need it. Fees are EUR 60 non-residential or EUR 75 residential, paid in advance, then each delegate registers individually through the form.
highlights: Selection route to EYP Ireland National Session and international sessions
Residential weekend with European volunteer chairs
Affordable: EUR 60-75
eyp-ireland-munster-regional-session-202.eligibility: Senior-cycle secondary-school students (about 15-18) in Ireland, in school delegations or individually. Officials from other countries apply via the EYP Members Platform.
how_to_apply: Ask your school to register a delegation or contact the head organisers
Pay the participation fee in advance
Register individually through the session registration form
Prepare with the topic overviews sent before the session
eyp-ireland-munster-regional-session-202.costs: EUR 60 non-residential / EUR 75 residential (accommodation Friday-Saturday). Late payment admin fee EUR 10; no refunds within a week of the session.

eyp-turkiye-university-forum-istanbul-20.about:
EYP Türkiye's University Forum brings the European Youth Parliament format to university-age participants: teambuilding, committee work on current European and global issues, and a General Assembly where resolutions are debated and voted, all in English. The 2026 edition starts on 10 December 2026 in Istanbul (check the event page for the exact end date and venue).

It is listed as open for applications on EYP Türkiye's events page and suits students in Istanbul or those who can travel there; experienced EYP alumni from any country can also volunteer as officials.
highlights: EYP-style debate for university students
Hosted in Istanbul
English-language committees
eyp-turkiye-university-forum-istanbul-20.eligibility: University students (18+); no nationality restriction stated. Language English.
how_to_apply: Open the EYP Türkiye events page
Click "Check Details & Apply" for University Forum 2026
Complete the application form and await confirmation
eyp-turkiye-university-forum-istanbul-20.costs: Participation fee set by EYP Türkiye; travel and accommodation not covered unless stated.

generation-euro-students-award-france-20.about:
Generation €uro is the Eurosystem's competition that teaches how the ECB sets interest rates. In France it is run by the Banque de France with the Ministry of Education for students in Première and Terminale. Teams of 3-5 students supervised by a teacher take an online quiz (5 Oct - 27 Nov 2026), selected teams submit a written presentation of a monetary-policy decision (7 Dec 2026 - 2 Feb 2027), and five finalist teams present orally at the Banque de France in Paris on 19 March 2027.

Free to enter; a strong project for students interested in economics, finance or international institutions.
highlights: Learn how the ECB sets monetary policy
Final at the Banque de France in Paris
Free; teams of 3-5 with a teacher
generation-euro-students-award-france-20.eligibility: Upper-secondary students (Première/Terminale) at schools in France, in teams of 3-5 supervised by a teacher.
how_to_apply: Form a team of 3-5 students with a supervising teacher
Register the team on the Generation €uro France site
Complete the online quiz by 27 Nov 2026
If selected, submit the written presentation by 2 Feb 2027
generation-euro-students-award-france-20.costs: Free. Travel to the Paris final is organised for finalists by the organisers (check brochure).

gyiif-2027.about:
Global Youth Invention and Innovation Fair (GYIIF) is an international science, invention and innovation fair run by the Indonesian Young Scientist Association (IYSA), which organises project competitions for students from elementary school to university in Indonesia and with partners in many countries. GYIIF is held in collaboration with the Department of Food Science and Technology of IPB University (Institut Pertanian Bogor).

Participants (individually or in small teams) submit a research or invention project in one of the categories (social science, environmental science, innovation science, life sciences, engineering and technology, physics) and present it to a panel of judges, either in person in Indonesia or online. Medals (gold, silver, bronze) and special awards are given, and all participants receive certificates.

It is an accessible way for school and university students to present their first research project internationally. The guidebook on the official website gives the venue, fees and rules.
highlights: Hybrid: compete online or in person in Indonesia
Open to elementary, secondary and university students
Medals, special awards and certificates
gyiif-2027.eligibility: Students from elementary school to university, from any country, individually or in teams with a supervisor (see guidebook for team size and age categories).
how_to_apply: Read the GYIIF guidebook on the official website.
Register online through the official registration link before the deadline.
Pay the registration fee for online or offline participation as set out in the guidebook.
Submit your project materials (abstract, poster/video) and present to the judges on the event dates.
gyiif-2027.costs: Registration fee varies by online or offline participation and nationality; see the official guidebook. Travel and accommodation for offline participants are self-funded.

i2aspo-2026.about:
Indonesia International Applied Science Project Olympiad (I2ASPO) is an international science, invention and innovation fair run by the Indonesian Young Scientist Association (IYSA), which organises project competitions for students from elementary school to university in Indonesia and with partners in many countries. I2ASPO challenges students to create work that can be applied directly to benefit society and to find solutions to problems in their own environment.

Participants (individually or in small teams) submit a research or invention project in one of the categories (waste treatment, IoT, functional food, energy, research on children with special needs, entrepreneurship, physics and engineering, applied social, environmental and life sciences) and present it to a panel of judges, either in person in Indonesia or online. Medals (gold, silver, bronze) and special awards are given, and all participants receive certificates.

It is an accessible way for school and university students to present their first research project internationally. The guidebook on the official website gives the venue, fees and rules.
highlights: Hybrid: compete online or in person in Indonesia
Open to elementary, secondary and university students
Medals, special awards and certificates
i2aspo-2026.eligibility: Students from elementary school to university, from any country, individually or in teams with a supervisor (see guidebook for team size and age categories).
how_to_apply: Read the I2ASPO guidebook on the official website.
Register online through the official registration link before the deadline.
Pay the registration fee for online or offline participation as set out in the guidebook.
Submit your project materials (abstract, poster/video) and present to the judges on the event dates.
i2aspo-2026.costs: Registration fee varies by online or offline participation and nationality; see the official guidebook. Travel and accommodation for offline participants are self-funded.

iasas-student-leader-global-summit-manil.about:
The Student Leader Global Summit (SLGS) is the annual student-leadership event of IASAS, the international association of university student-affairs professionals. The 2027 summit is hosted in Manila, Philippines, by the Philippine Association of Campus Student Advisers (PACSA) from 26 to 29 May 2027 (the 2026 edition was in Hong Kong).

It brings together student leaders (student union, club and residence leaders and other active students) to connect across cultures, exchange ideas and develop leadership. Staff from your university's student-affairs office can accompany you.

In 2026 the fee (about EUR 290–320) covered three nights' accommodation, meals and materials; the 2027 fee is still to be confirmed.
highlights: Meet student leaders from universities worldwide
Hosted by the Philippine student-affairs association
Accommodation and meals included in the package (2026 model)
iasas-student-leader-global-summit-manil.eligibility: University students active in student leadership; applicants usually apply with the support of their university student-affairs office.
how_to_apply: Open the SLGS Manila 2027 page on iasas.global and click 'Students apply now'.
Submit your application (reviews begin January 2027).
Confirm your place within a couple of weeks of acceptance.
Pay the registration fee a month before the event and book flights.
iasas-student-leader-global-summit-manil.costs: Registration fee not yet confirmed (2026: EUR 290 members / EUR 320 non-members, including 3 nights, meals and materials). Flights extra.

icas-assessments-2027.about:
ICAS (originally the International Competitions and Assessments for Schools, developed at UNSW) are annual academic competitions sat online at school. Subjects are Mathematics, English, Science, Writing, Digital Technologies and the Spelling Bee, for students from Year 2 to Year 12.

In 2026 the sitting windows ran through August (Digital Technologies and Writing 3–7 Aug, English 10–14 Aug, Science 17–21 Aug, Mathematics 24–28 Aug), with entries closing in late July. The 2027 calendar is expected to follow the same pattern.

Every student receives a detailed individual report; top performers receive High Distinction certificates and medals. Schools in Australia, New Zealand, Asia and other regions take part, and parents can enter through the school's parent payment system.
highlights: Six subjects for Years 2–12
Detailed skills report for every student
Medals for top scorers internationally
icas-assessments-2027.eligibility: School students in Years 2–12 at participating schools (Australia, New Zealand, Asia and elsewhere; India via a separate ICAS India site). Entry is through the school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it runs ICAS, or ask it to register.
Enter through the school or the Parent Payment System before the July closing date.
Sit each subject online at school in its August window.
Receive results and certificates later in the year.
icas-assessments-2027.costs: 2026: from AUD 21.95 per student per subject; 2027 fees to be published.

iqc-useqip-2027.about:
USEQIP is a two-week summer school run every year since 2009 by the Institute for Quantum Computing (IQC) at the University of Waterloo, Canada. It is aimed mainly at students one year away from finishing their undergraduate degree in physics, engineering, chemistry, mathematics or computer science. Lectures by IQC faculty cover quantum algorithms, error correction, cryptography, decoherence and the physical implementations of quantum computers; this is followed by more than 30 hours of experiments in IQC's labs, including NMR quantum control, entangled photon sources, superconducting devices, nanofabrication in the cleanroom and quantum key distribution.

USEQIP 2027 runs 31 May – 11 June 2027 with space for about 30 students, in person only. It is free and travel bursaries are available. Participants are encouraged to stay on for a paid summer Undergraduate Research Award (URA) with IQC researchers; international students are only considered for USEQIP if they also apply for a URA (one combined application).
highlights: Hands-on experiments with real quantum hardware at a world-leading institute
No cost, with travel bursaries
Can be combined with a paid summer research award at IQC
iqc-useqip-2027.eligibility: Undergraduate students, ideally one year from completing their degree, in physics, engineering, chemistry, mathematics, computer science or related fields (all interested students may apply). Open to international students, who must apply for USEQIP together with a summer Undergraduate Research Award. Attendance must be in person in Waterloo.
how_to_apply: Complete the USEQIP 2027 online application by 3 January 2027 (indicate URA interest; mandatory for international applicants)
Upload a CV, a cover letter (addressing USEQIP and the URA) and an unofficial transcript
Arrange one reference, due by 6 January 2027
Decisions are emailed by 31 January 2027; arrange a Canadian visa/eTA if selected
iqc-useqip-2027.costs: Free; travel bursaries available. The optional Undergraduate Research Award is a paid summer research position.

kansai-university-ijlc-summer-2027.about:
Kansai University's IJLC programme runs two three-week summer courses near Osaka: Summer 1 in June and Summer 2 in July (in 2026: 2–25 June and 30 June – 23 July). Classes are taught in Japanese at three levels: Primary (about JLPT N5; you must already read and type hiragana and katakana), Intermediate (N4–N3) and Intermediate-Advanced (N2+), with cultural activities.

It is open to foreign nationals currently enrolled at a college or university, or who graduated within one year before the course starts; capacity is about 45 per session.

Applications close about two and a half months before each session, or earlier when full, so apply as soon as the 2027 course guide is published.
highlights: Three levels from beginner to advanced
Two sessions to choose from (June or July)
Open to any foreign university student or recent graduate
kansai-university-ijlc-summer-2027.eligibility: Foreign nationals enrolled at a college/university or graduated within one year of the course start. Beginners must know hiragana and katakana.
how_to_apply: Download the IJLC Course Guide for 2027 fees and dates.
Choose Summer 1 (June) or Summer 2 (July) and your level.
Apply online before the deadline (about 2.5 months ahead) or before seats fill.
Pay fees and arrange accommodation and visa.
kansai-university-ijlc-summer-2027.costs: Fees depend on length of stay and accommodation type (see the official Course Guide).

kyung-hee-global-collaborative-summer-20.about:
The Global Collaborative (GC) Summer Program at Kyung Hee University, Seoul, offers English-taught, credit-bearing courses under the theme 'Humanity, Civilization and Global Governance', many taught by visiting professors from leading universities abroad.

Students from KHU partner universities and non-partner universities worldwide can join; students enrolled outside Korea pay overseas rates. Optional dormitory rooms and a Korean culture experience package are available.

The 2027 dates and application window will be published on the GC site (the 2026 cycle closed in June).
highlights: Courses by international visiting professors
Up to 6 transferable credits
Optional dorm and Korean culture package
kyung-hee-global-collaborative-summer-20.eligibility: University students from partner and non-partner universities worldwide (see the GC site for detailed requirements).
how_to_apply: Check summer.khu.ac.kr for the 2027 academic calendar.
Apply online and pay the KRW 100,000 application fee.
Pay tuition (and optional dorm/culture fees) by the payment deadline.
Email the payment receipt to summer@khu.ac.kr.
kyung-hee-global-collaborative-summer-20.costs: 2026 overseas rates: application KRW 100,000; tuition KRW 1,600,000 (3 credits) or KRW 2,300,000 (up to 6 credits); dorm KRW 600,000; culture activities KRW 450,000.

lxmls-lisbon-machine-learning-school-202.about:
The Lisbon Machine Learning School (LxMLS) has run every July since 2011 at the Congress Centre of Instituto Superior Técnico (IST) in Lisbon. It combines morning lectures on machine learning, deep learning and natural language processing by well-known researchers from academia and industry with afternoon lab sessions where participants implement the methods in Python, plus a poster session and social events. The 2026 edition (the 16th) ran 20–25 July 2026, back-to-back with the ELLIS Doctoral Symposium.

The school is intended for graduate students and researchers in NLP, computational linguistics, computer science and statistics, and for industry practitioners; strong undergraduates with programming and maths background also apply. Admission is selective via an online application. A limited number of scholarships, funded by sponsors, cover the registration fee and sometimes travel and lodging for students worldwide who could not otherwise attend.
highlights: Lectures by leading ML/NLP researchers plus daily hands-on labs
Held at IST in central Lisbon with poster session and banquet
Scholarships for talented students from anywhere
lxmls-lisbon-machine-learning-school-202.eligibility: Graduate students (master's/PhD), researchers and industry practitioners in machine learning, NLP, computational linguistics, computer science or statistics; advanced undergraduates with solid maths and Python skills may apply. Open to all nationalities (participants handle their own Schengen visa).
how_to_apply: Watch lxmls.it.pt for the 2027 call (expected early 2027)
Submit the online application form by the deadline (8 May in 2026); tick the scholarship option if you need funding
Admission results come about ten days later (18 May in 2026)
If accepted, register and pay (early or late rate) and book accommodation separately
lxmls-lisbon-machine-learning-school-202.costs: Registration (2026 rates, early/late): EUR 400/450 for students, EUR 450/550 for professors and public-institute researchers, EUR 650/750 for others; covers lectures, labs, lunches, coffee breaks and the banquet. Accommodation and travel extra. Limited scholarships cover the fee and possibly travel/lodging.

mahidol-muic-summer-program-2027.about:
The MUIC Summer Program runs on Mahidol University's Salaya campus near Bangkok from 1 to 30 July 2027. Option 1, 'Sustainable in Actions', is an all-day Practical Sustainability and Biodiversity course with overnight field visits. Option 2 offers 4-credit courses: The Psychology of Emotional Well-being, Perspectives on Thailand, Introduction to Thai Language and Culture, Diversity and Expatriate Management, International Design Language and Culture, Introduction to Tropical Medicine, and Social and Health Issues in Thailand.

It is open to undergraduates who have completed at least one semester (or recent graduates) from any university worldwide. Extras include Muay Thai, Thai cooking and dance, a day trip to Ayutthaya, airport transfers, and help with visa letters and housing.

Courses earn a digital transcript, so credits can often be transferred to your home university.
highlights: Credit-bearing courses including tropical medicine and global health
Open to undergraduates from any university
Cultural programme: Muay Thai, Thai cooking, Ayutthaya trip
mahidol-muic-summer-program-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates who have completed at least one semester, or recent graduates, from any country. IELTS 5.5 or equivalent for non-native English speakers (or a recommendation letter from an English professor).
how_to_apply: Fill in the online application form on the MUIC Summer Program page (from 1 November 2026).
Upload passport page, transcript, English proof (or recommendation) and photo.
Pay the invoice within 15 days and email proof to icshortterm@mahidol.ac.th.
Receive the acceptance and visa letters from MUIC.
mahidol-muic-summer-program-2027.costs: Option 1: THB 82,500 (about USD 2,500) including shared accommodation. Option 2: THB 33,500 for one course or THB 62,000 for two (accommodation not included). Fees include tuition, visits, transcript, airport transfers and welcome/farewell meals; flights and insurance extra.

miami-summer-scholars-2027.about:
The University of Miami's Summer Scholars Program is a three-week pre-college programme (26 June – 16 July 2027) in which current high-school sophomores and juniors take a university course for college credit, taught by UM faculty, in fields such as forensics, microbiology, tropical marine biology, engineering, health and business. Students live on the Coral Gables campus, take part in college-prep workshops and explore South Florida on field trips and weekend excursions; almost 600 high-school students took part in a recent summer.

Alongside it, the two-week non-credit UM Academies (26 June – 9 July 2027) are open to 9th–11th graders, including the Shark Academy with UM's Shark Research and Conservation Program, an entrepreneurship venture challenge, and intensive English courses for English-language learners. Applications for summer 2027 open on 1 November 2026.
highlights: Earn University of Miami credit in three weeks
Marine-science options such as the Shark Academy
Intensive English academies for international students
miami-summer-scholars-2027.eligibility: Summer Scholars: current high-school sophomores and juniors (10th–11th grade). UM Academies: 9th–11th graders. International students can apply (the intensive English academies are designed for English-language learners); check visa requirements for the US.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply online from 1 November 2026
Choose Summer Scholars (credit) or a UM Academy (non-credit) and your course
Submit transcripts and any requested recommendations/essays
Apply early: places are limited and fill before summer
miami-summer-scholars-2027.costs: Paid programme; 2027 tuition and residential fees are shown on the UM Pre-College tuition page when applications open. Travel and visa costs extra.

model-european-parliament-65th-imep-vien.about:
The Model European Parliament (MEP), founded in 1994, is a leadership programme that brings high-school students from the 27 EU member states, candidate and guest countries together twice a year for an international session. The 65th iMEP takes place in Vienna from 10 to 17 March 2027, organised by MEP Austria. Delegates work in committees modelled on the European Parliament, draft resolutions and defend them in a General Assembly, with a cultural and social programme alongside.

Countries send national delegations, usually chosen at national MEP sessions or through participating schools; candidate countries such as Ukraine, Moldova, Georgia, Serbia, Albania, Montenegro and North Macedonia have taken part. Working language English.
highlights: International session with delegations from 30+ countries
Hosted by MEP Austria in Vienna
Committee work, General Assembly and cultural programme
model-european-parliament-65th-imep-vien.eligibility: Secondary-school students (about 15-19) selected for their national MEP delegation through a participating school or national session. Working language English.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it takes part in the Model European Parliament, or contact your national MEP coordinator (list on the MEP Europe site)
Get selected for your school/national delegation (often via a national session)
Your teacher registers the delegation; you complete the student registration with the link you receive
Prepare your committee topic before the session
model-european-parliament-65th-imep-vien.costs: Participation fee and travel set by the national organisation/school; host families or group accommodation usually arranged by the host.

model-european-parliament-66th-imep-wars.about:
The 66th iMEP takes place in Warsaw from 2 to 9 June 2027 (listed on MEP Europe's session page). As at every international MEP session, national delegations of high-school students debate European issues in parliamentary committees, write resolutions and vote on them in a General Assembly, while getting to know the host city and each other's cultures.

Delegations are chosen nationally - typically at a national MEP session or by participating schools - so contact your country's MEP coordinator or ask your school early.
highlights: International MEP session in Warsaw
Debate EU policy with students from 30+ countries
Path from national sessions to international level
model-european-parliament-66th-imep-wars.eligibility: Secondary-school students (about 15-19) selected for their national MEP delegation. Working language English.

Get selected for your school/national delegation (often via a national session)

Prepare your committee topic before the session
model-european-parliament-66th-imep-wars.costs: Participation fee and travel set by the national organisation/school; host families or group accommodation usually arranged by the host.

model-european-parliament-austria-nation.about:
The 26th national Model European Parliament of Austria takes place in Schwaz and Innsbruck, Tyrol, from 14 to 17 January 2027, in English. Delegations from Austrian schools debate in parliamentary committees and a General Assembly; national sessions are where many countries choose delegates for international MEP sessions such as the 65th iMEP in Vienna.

Contact MEP Austria (via its Facebook/Instagram listed on the MEP Europe site) or your school's MEP coordinator to join.
highlights: English-language national session in Tyrol
Feeds into international sessions (iMEP Vienna 2027 is hosted by MEP Austria)
Four days of committee work and debate

Prepare your committee topic before the session
model-european-parliament-austria-nation.costs: Participation fee and travel set by the national organisation/school; host families or group accommodation usually arranged by the host.

model-european-parliament-belgium-nation.about:
MEP Belgium organises a national Model European Parliament session from 21 to 26 February 2027, with the General Assembly held in the European Parliament in Brussels. Students form committees, research a European issue, write a resolution and defend it in the plenary - a rare chance to debate inside the real hemicycle.

The session is run in Flemish/Dutch for Belgian secondary schools; MEP Belgium also sends delegations to international sessions (iMEP, WEMEP, EUROMEP, MEP BSR).
highlights: General Assembly inside the European Parliament
Route to international MEP sessions
Run by MEP Belgium

model-european-parliament-germany-nation.about:
MEP Germany runs its 28th national Model European Parliament from 20 to 25 March 2027 (in German), as listed on the MEP Europe homepage. School delegations debate European issues in committees and a closing General Assembly; the national session is the usual route into German delegations for international MEP sessions.

The host city is announced by MEP Germany (contact via its Facebook/Instagram linked from the MEP Europe national organisers page). City coordinates here are indicative.
highlights: Six-day German-language national session
Selection route to international MEP sessions
Run by MEP Germany

model-european-parliament-malta-national.about:
Malta's national Model European Parliament session takes place on 9-10 January 2027 (English/Maltese), as listed by MEP Europe. Students from Maltese schools take on the role of MEPs, debate in committees and vote resolutions in a General Assembly.

National sessions are the usual route into Malta's delegations for international and Mediterranean (EUROMEP) sessions. Ask your school or the national MEP coordinator to take part.
highlights: Short national session in English and Maltese
Route to international and Mediterranean MEP sessions
Practise EU debate and resolution writing
model-european-parliament-malta-national.eligibility: Secondary-school students in Malta via participating schools.

model-european-parliament-wemep-norwich-.about:
WEMEP is the Western European Region's annual Model European Parliament session, with around ten countries per session so that more students can take part than at the international sessions. The 2027 edition is hosted in Norwich/Norfolk, UK, in February 2027 (MEP Europe lists 13-19 Feb, to be confirmed; MEP Belgium lists 13-20 Feb).

School delegations debate in committees and a General Assembly, live with peers from other countries and explore the region. Participation is via schools linked to the national MEP organisations of the Western European Region.
highlights: Smaller regional session, more places per country
Hosted in Norwich, UK
Committee work and General Assembly in English
model-european-parliament-wemep-norwich-.eligibility: Secondary-school students from participating schools in Western European MEP countries (e.g. Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, UK, Germany, France).
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it takes part in the Model European Parliament, or contact your national MEP coordinator (list on the MEP Europe site)
Get selected for your school/national delegation (often via a national session)
Your teacher registers the delegation; you complete the student registration with the link you receive
Prepare your committee topic before the session
model-european-parliament-wemep-norwich-.costs: Participation fee and travel set by the national organisation/school; host families or group accommodation usually arranged by the host.

nus-hack-and-roll-2027.about:
Hack&Roll is an annual 24-hour hackathon organised by NUS Hackers, the student hacker club of the National University of Singapore. Teams of 1–4 build any project they like over a weekend, with workshops, food, swag and prizes for the best hacks; it returns in January 2027.

It is open to students from primary school to graduate level, including pre-university students; graduate students and graduates may take part but are not eligible for prizes. International participants are welcome, but the organisers do not help with visas, travel or accommodation, so it is most practical for students in or visiting Singapore.

Registrations are reviewed and not everyone is accepted, so register early when the form opens.
highlights: Free, with food and swag
Beginner-friendly: any project, teams of 1–4
Prizes for the top teams
nus-hack-and-roll-2027.eligibility: Students from primary school to graduate studies (graduate students/graduates not prize-eligible). International participants welcome but must arrange their own travel and stay.
how_to_apply: Watch hacknroll.nushackers.org for the 2027 registration form.
Register individually or as a team (teams of 1–4 are formed after acceptance).
Wait for the acceptance email.
Attend the 24-hour hackathon at NUS and demo your project for judging.
nus-hack-and-roll-2027.costs: Free. Food provided. Travel and accommodation are your own.

okayama-university-jv-campus-online-cour.about:
Okayama University's JV-Campus Course 3, 'Driving the Setouchi Art Movement Toward a Circular Society', is a fully online, on-demand course of 14 video lectures (about 35 minutes each) running from 4 December 2026 to 2 February 2027. It explores how contemporary art in the Seto Inland Sea islands revitalises communities and supports sustainability.

It is free for students enrolled in a regular programme at an Okayama University partner institution. All completers receive a transcript, and the course can count as one credit if you later enrol in an Okayama undergraduate programme.

Apply via the online form by 12 November 2026, 5pm JST; missing deadlines for viewing or assignments results in an F grade.
highlights: Free online course from a Japanese national university
Transcript issued; credit can count towards Okayama degrees
Art, community revitalisation and sustainability
okayama-university-jv-campus-online-cour.eligibility: Students enrolled in a regular programme at an Okayama University partner institution, remaining enrolled until the course ends. Priority to those who completed the earlier courses.
how_to_apply: Check that your university is an Okayama University partner.
Submit the Microsoft Forms application linked on the JV-Campus page by 12 November 2026, 5pm JST.
Receive the approval notice within a week after the deadline.
Watch all lectures and submit assignments on time.
okayama-university-jv-campus-online-cour.costs: Free for students at partner institutions.

oxford-university-summer-school-for-adul.about:
The Oxford University Summer School for Adults (OUSSA) is run by the University of Oxford's Department for Continuing Education at Rewley House in central Oxford. In 2027 it runs in six one-week blocks from 3 July to 14 August; participants pick one or more week-long courses from a list of 60+ in literature, creative writing, history, archaeology, architecture, history of art, philosophy, theology, psychology and biological sciences. Each week has morning seminars of no more than 12 students, two one-to-one tutorials, guest lectures, access to the Bodleian library and a social programme.

It is open to anyone aged 18 or over (students, graduates and lifelong learners) of any nationality. Each course carries 10 CATS credits at undergraduate level (FHEQ Level 4) for students who attend all classes and complete a 1,000-word assignment or presentation; a 1,500-word pre-course assignment is compulsory. Non-native speakers need strong English (IELTS 7.5 with 7.0 in each part, or equivalent, unless waived). Residential places include room and all meals; non-residential places include lunch and dinner.
highlights: Week-long Oxford courses taught in seminars of max. 12
10 CATS credits per course plus two one-to-one tutorials
Open to all adults 18+, residential or non-residential
oxford-university-summer-school-for-adul.eligibility: Anyone aged 18 or over, any nationality. Non-native English speakers must show IELTS Academic 7.5 (7.0 in each component), TOEFL iBT 110 or C1 Advanced 191, unless they recently studied a degree in English. Visa or UK ETA as required.
how_to_apply: Browse the 2027 course list and check each course page for its fee
Enrol online (pay in full by card) or submit an application form
Book before 30 April 2027; join the waiting list if a course is full
Complete the 1,500-word pre-course assignment (due early June)
Arrange a visa or UK ETA; request an enrolment letter after paying
oxford-university-summer-school-for-adul.costs: Fees are charged per person per week and listed on each course page (tuition plus meals; residential option includes accommodation in Wellington Square). Concessionary non-residential rates exist for those who qualify. Travel and insurance extra.

parma-eyc2027-digital-energy-nexus-acade.about:
Part of the official programme of Parma European Youth Capital 2027, this international academy (25-29 October 2027) examines the intersection of the digital and energy transitions: the energy demand of data centres, waste-heat recovery and district heating, smart grids, demand forecasting, machine learning and Model Predictive Control. It includes a technical visit to the Qarnot data centre and A2A infrastructure in Brescia and a visit to the campus thermal plant.

Young researchers and students work in groups and present policy-oriented recommendations publicly on the last day. Activities are in English. Registration opens 20 November 2026 on the academy page; 18 mobility grants cover travel and stay for participants from outside Parma.
highlights: 18 mobility grants for travel and accommodation
Technical visits to a data centre and district-heating network
English-language programme with international experts
parma-eyc2027-digital-energy-nexus-acade.eligibility: Students, young researchers and young professionals (engineering/energy/data backgrounds suit best); Italian and international participants welcome. English.
how_to_apply: Open the academy page on the University of Parma site
From 20 November 2026, fill in the registration form on that page
If you live outside Parma, request one of the mobility grants (travel and stay)
Wait for confirmation from the organisers
parma-eyc2027-digital-energy-nexus-acade.costs: Participation is by registration; 18 mobility grants cover travel and accommodation for participants from outside Parma.

parma-eyc2027-food-city-design-academy.about:
Food City Design, part of Parma European Youth Capital 2027 (Piazza of Food), trains young graduates to connect public administrations, businesses, agri-food supply chains, food and wine tourism and citizens. Five online days cover urban food systems, sustainability, tourism and local development, community wellbeing, and culture and creativity; participants then spend five days on an individual or group project with an academic tutor.

The final phase is in person at Laboratorio Aperto in Parma (28 June - 1 July 2027), with a stakeholder workshop and a cultural and gastronomic visit; projects feed into Parma's Food Policy and a published booklet. In English. Registration opens 20 November 2026; 20 mobility grants available.
highlights: 20 mobility grants
Projects feed into Parma's real Food Policy
In Parma, a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy
parma-eyc2027-food-city-design-academy.eligibility: Young graduates (and similar profiles) interested in food systems, sustainability, tourism or urban policy; international participants welcome. English.
how_to_apply: Open the academy page on the University of Parma site
From 20 November 2026, fill in the registration form on that page
If you live outside Parma, request one of the mobility grants (travel and stay)
Wait for confirmation from the organisers
parma-eyc2027-food-city-design-academy.costs: Participation is by registration; 20 mobility grants cover travel and accommodation for participants from outside Parma.

parma-eyc2027-livinglab-piazze-in-movime.about:
Parma LivingLab Academy invites students, young researchers and professionals to rethink eight of Parma's public squares as comfortable, inclusive and shared spaces. Over an intensive week (24-28 May 2027) participants do site visits and mapping, learn co-design, tactical urbanism and AI-enabled participation tools, meet experts and the city administration, and turn their ideas into a 'Piazza Activation Toolkit' presented to the Municipality and community.

Themes: social and civic life, pedestrian-first space, climate adaptation and universal design. All activities are in English. Registration opens 20 November 2026; 10 mobility grants for participants from outside Parma.
highlights: Real urban-design project with the city of Parma
10 mobility grants
English-language international school
parma-eyc2027-livinglab-piazze-in-movime.eligibility: Students, young researchers and young professionals in architecture, planning, design, social sciences and related fields; international participants welcome. English.

parma-eyc2027-responsible-ai-at-work-aca.about:
This Academy at the University of Parma's Department of Economics and Management (9-10 September 2027) covers how AI works, data management and ethical issues on day one, and applications in business on day two: group design challenges on data analysis, content production and innovation, ethical-dilemma role plays and discussions with companies, cooperatives, IT firms and labour representatives.

Outputs feed into a Responsible AI Manifesto for Parma European Youth Capital 2027. In English; registration opens 20 November 2026; 10 mobility grants for participants from outside Parma.
highlights: Hands-on design challenges with real business cases
Networking with companies and young professionals
10 mobility grants
parma-eyc2027-responsible-ai-at-work-aca.eligibility: Students and young professionals interested in AI, business or management; international participants welcome. English.

If you live outside Parma, request one of the mobility grants (travel and stay)

parma-eyc2027-starther-womens-entreprene.about:
StartHER supports female students, PhD candidates, researchers and young entrepreneurs under 35 in developing a business project, with a focus on closing the gender gap in entrepreneurship. Over three days (13-15 April 2027) it combines lectures on the economic, financial and communication sides of starting a business with a practical lab using Design Thinking, Business Model Canvas and Lean Canvas, supported by mentors.

Participants pitch to a technical committee; the strongest projects are showcased at PURE - Parma University Research & Entrepreneurship. Registration opens 20 November 2026; 15 mobility grants for participants from outside Parma. Check the page for working language.

Mentoring and pitch to a technical committee
15 mobility grants

pembroke-cambridge-summer-programme-2027.about:
The Pembroke Cambridge Summer Programme is run by Pembroke College itself, one of the oldest colleges of the University of Cambridge. From 10 July to 21 August 2027 students live in the college and take three courses across two modules, taught in small lectures and seminars by Cambridge-affiliated academics. The 2027 portfolio covers economics, politics and international relations, history, literature, film, neuroscience, public health, cyber security, materials science and more; students planning research can replace one course with an Independent Supervision Research Project with one-to-one supervision.

It is open to university students worldwide who will have completed at least their first year of university by July 2027, with a GPA of at least 3.2/4.0 (3.5 recommended) or equivalent and a high level of English. Applications are rolling, so earlier applicants get the cheaper rooms. An official transcript is issued for credit transfer. Pembroke does not offer general financial aid (its small 1976 Scholarships are only for University of California students).
highlights: Run by Pembroke College, University of Cambridge
Small-group teaching, three courses or a one-to-one research project
Six weeks living and dining in a historic Cambridge college
pembroke-cambridge-summer-programme-2027.eligibility: University students (any nationality) who will have completed at least one year of undergraduate study by the start; minimum GPA 3.2/4.0 or equivalent; high English proficiency (see the English requirements page). Under-18s are not the target group.
how_to_apply: Check with your own university's study abroad office whether you must apply through it
Create an account in Pembroke's online application system once it opens (early November 2026)
Submit the form with a personal statement and have your university send an official transcript
If accepted, pay the GBP 600 accommodation deposit and choose courses and room band by 3 June 2027
Apply for a UK visa or ETA if required
pembroke-cambridge-summer-programme-2027.costs: 2027 fees: application fee GBP 60; tuition GBP 6,450; accommodation and meal credit GBP 2,900–4,100 depending on room band (6 weeks); optional Independent Supervision supplement GBP 1,670. Flights, visa and insurance extra. No financial aid from the college.

raisina-dialogue-2027-student-registrati.about:
The Raisina Dialogue is India's premier conference on geopolitics and geoeconomics, held annually in New Delhi since 2016 by the Observer Research Foundation in partnership with India's Ministry of External Affairs. The 2027 edition runs from 18 to 20 March 2027.

Over three days, heads of state and government, ministers, policymakers, business leaders, academics and journalists debate foreign policy, technology, climate and security in plenaries and panels. It is one of the best places in Asia for students of international relations, economics and public policy to hear world leaders in person and network.

Registration is open now, with separate categories for Indian residents, international registrants, students and media; students should register in the student category.
highlights: Hear world leaders and ministers in person
One of Asia's biggest foreign-policy conferences
Dedicated student registration category
raisina-dialogue-2027-student-registrati.eligibility: University students of any nationality interested in international affairs (register under the Students category; student ID likely required). International attendees need an Indian visa.
how_to_apply: Open the Raisina Dialogue page on orfonline.org and choose the Students registration category.
Create an account on the ORF event platform and complete the form.
Wait for confirmation of your registration.
Arrange travel and an Indian visa (if needed) for 18–20 March 2027.
raisina-dialogue-2027-student-registrati.costs: Registration terms (and any fee) are shown on the ORF registration platform. Travel, visa and accommodation are at your own cost.

santa-fe-institute-undergraduate-complex.about:
The Santa Fe Institute (SFI) in New Mexico is a world-leading centre for complexity science. Its Undergraduate Complexity Research (UCR) programme brings undergraduates from the physical, natural and social sciences and mathematics to SFI for ten weeks (30 May – 7 August 2027) to carry out an independent research project with an SFI mentor, alongside lectures, workshops and the institute's interdisciplinary community. It is a full-time, in-person programme.

Participants receive a USD 7,000 stipend, free housing and meals during the residential stay, and travel support to and from Santa Fe. International students are welcome: those at US institutions usually join on F-1 CPT, and those enrolled outside the US are also eligible, with SFI possibly sponsoring a J-1 visa. Strong quantitative or programming skills are favoured; priority usually goes to students entering their junior or senior year.
highlights: Independent research project with a mentor at a world-leading complexity institute
USD 7,000 stipend plus free housing, meals and travel support
Open to international undergraduates, including those studying outside the US (J-1 support possible)
santa-fe-institute-undergraduate-complex.eligibility: Current undergraduates (associate's or bachelor's) who will still be enrolled for at least one term after August 2027, in physical, natural or social sciences or mathematics. Students who finish their degree before the programme ends are not eligible. Participants must be authorised to work in the US (international students via CPT or a J-1 sponsored by SFI where possible).
how_to_apply: Apply through SFI's SurveyMonkey Apply portal from early November 2026
Upload a current academic CV and unofficial transcripts (with English cover translation if needed)
Answer two research-statement prompts, including a short project proposal
Arrange one recommendation letter from a professor or mentor
Submit by 13 January 2027, 4 pm MST
santa-fe-institute-undergraduate-complex.costs: No fees. USD 7,000 stipend, free housing and meals during the residential programme, and travel support to and from Santa Fe.

sjtu-sdg-july-camp-2027.about:
The SDG July Camp brings students from around the world to Shanghai Jiao Tong University to tackle sustainability challenges through the UN Sustainable Development Goals, with support from UNDP. Students choose one of several SDG-themed courses taught through group projects, discussions and public lectures by global experts.

The camp also includes an opening ceremony and icebreakers, weekly cross-cultural activities and a closing ceremony where each course presents its report. Completers receive a certificate and an SJTU transcript.

In 2026 applications ran from 15 January to 31 May, with admission decisions in early June and the opening ceremony on 14 July; the 2027 camp is expected on the same calendar.
highlights: SDG-focused, project-based courses with SJTU transcript
Supported by UNDP
Cultural activities in Shanghai
sjtu-sdg-july-camp-2027.eligibility: University students from around the world interested in the SDGs (see the call for any GPA or language requirements).
how_to_apply: Check the SDG July Camp page for the 2027 course list (from January 2027).
Apply online at apply.sjtu.edu.cn before the end of May.
Wait for the admission decision (early June).
Apply for a Chinese visa with the admission documents.
sjtu-sdg-july-camp-2027.costs: Fees are listed in the yearly call (not shown on the overview page). Travel and visa extra.
